stories.headline: India may miss target of achieving exports worth $1 trillion during 2026-27 due to global uncertainties and tariff war, says NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri
stories.title: India may miss target of achieving exports worth $1 trillion during 2026-27 due to global uncertainties and tariff war, says NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri
stories.summary: Lahiri pointed out that the country needs to diversify its export basket, “States of origin” and export destinations in order to grow its shipments amid geopolitical uncertainties.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India may miss its ambitious target of achieving exports worth $1 trillion during 2026-27 due to the global uncertainties in general and tariff war in particular, according to NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri.
Lahiri pointed out that the country needs to diversify its export basket, “States of origin” and export destinations in order to grow its shipments amid geopolitical uncertainties.
“India’s exports are heavily concentrated in a small group of product categories, led by engineering goods, refined petroleum, electronics, gems and jewellery, and pharmaceuticals.
Moreover, just five States-- Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh generating nearly 70 percent of the country’s total shipments.
We need to diversify both our export basket as well as our States of origin and export destinations,” Lahiri said during an event of Bandhan Bank in Kolkata on Sunday evening.

The NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman said rising exports will help India modernise its technology and product quality, and also help the country in integrating with the global value chain and attract foreign investment.
Notably, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal in May said India has set a target of achieving exports worth USD 1 trillion this year and $2 trillion over the next five years.

Due to geopolitical risks and uncertainties, Indian exports were affected, and its trade gap widened in July as imports grew faster than exports, with the combined merchandise and services deficit rising 31.5 percent year-on-year to slightly over $15 billion, Lahiri said.
“India had set an ambitious target to reach $1 trillion in total combined exports of goods and services for 2026-27.
This goal may be missed due to the global uncertainties in general and tariff war in particular, and has been rolled forward to 2027-28,” Lahiri said.
He further said compounding or festering the geopolitical and tariff war tensions has resulted in stress in financial markets.
The disruption in world supply of oil, gas, and fertiliser has led to significant stiffening of their prices.

stories.headline: ‘One Nation, One Election’ proposal is ‘unconstitutional’: Chidambaram to parliament panel
stories.title: ‘One Nation, One Election’ proposal is ‘unconstitutional’: Chidambaram to parliament panel
stories.summary: We sought Chidambaram’s views as part of this examination process, and the committee will examine them before making its recommendations, said P.P. Chaudhary
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Former Union minister P. Chidambaram on Monday (August 24, 2026) strongly opposed the proposed move to hold simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State assemblies before a joint committee of Parliament, decrying the initiative as "monstrous" and "unconstitutional." The former Home and Finance Minister also said that the proposal to hold nationwide polls under "One Nation, One Election" is a "mindless" exercise.

Sources said Mr. Chidambaram submitted his opinion while appearing before the joint committee of Parliament on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which aim to synchronise Lok Sabha and State assembly polls.
The committee is headed by BJP member P.P. Chaudhary.
The senior Congress leader contended that the bills on simultaneous polls are "unconstitutional".
He argued that since any legislature is elected for a five-year term, curtailing its tenure directly violates the basic structure of the Constitution, sources aware of the deliberations said.

The senior Congress leader also said that his conscience does not allow him to support the bills and stressed that the government does not have the number (two-thirds majority) to pass the legislation, sources said.
TMC's Sagarika Ghosh, a member of the panel, also opposed the bill, claiming it would give "unbridled" power to the Election Commission.
When asked about Mr. Chidambaram's submission, Mr. Chaudhary said the former Union minister gave good inputs, but he may have a different view as he represents a particular party.
"The committee has been tasked by Parliament to examine and make recommendations.
We sought Chidambaram's views as part of this examination process, and the committee will examine them before making its recommendations," he said.
Mr. Chaudhary also asserted that the move to hold simultaneous elections is not against the basic structure of the Constitution.
A group of about 10 Padma awardees, including Tarlochan Singh, Navin Khanna, Meenakshi Jain and Niru Kumar, also appeared separately before the panel.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Restores Congress Leaders Petition Challenging BJP MP's Election From Assam
stories.title: Supreme Court Restores Congress Leaders Petition Challenging BJP MP's Election From Assam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (August 24) restored an election petition filed by advocate and Indian National Congress member Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury, challenging the election of Bharatiya Janata Party's Kripanath Mallah, who won the Lok Sabha elections from the No. 7 Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency in Assam during the 2024 General Elections.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran allowed the civil appeal, which has been preferred under Section 116A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, challenging the Gauhati High Court's judgment dated April 4, 2025, which rejected the election petition at the threshold.

By the said judgment, the High Court had dismissed the election petition filed by Choudhary challenging the election of Kripanath, alleging corrupt practices within the meaning of Section 123 of the RP Act.

However, the returned candidate filed an application under Section 86, read with Sections 81 and 83 of the RoP Act, and Section 151 CPC, seeking the outright dismissal of the election petition at the threshold, without going into a full trial.
This was allowed by the High Court.
Choudhury had contested the 2024 parliamentary election from the Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency.
As recorded in the appeal papers, the appellant had secured 5,26,733 votes, while the returned candidate had secured 5,45,093 votes, the difference being 18,360 votes.
Justice Chandran pronounced the judgment as: "Relying on the earlier Constitution Bench judgment, we have allowed the appeal."
Detailed judgment awaited.

stories.headline: Sajad Lone slams CM Omar over his power tariff hike remark, says ‘comparisons were not made during elections’
stories.title: Sajad Lone slams CM Omar over his power tariff hike remark, says ‘comparisons were not made during elections’
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 24: Peoples’ Conference chairman and MLA Handwara Sajad Gani Lone on Monday slammed chief minister Omar Abdullah over his remark on recent power tariff hike in which the latter stated that “he never promised that rates wouldn’t increase”. Lone highlighted that chief minister didn’t make such comparisons during elections when he sought votes from the people of Jammu and Kashmir. On Monday, chief minister Omar Abdullah while replying to the queries of reporters said that his government had never promised that power rates would not rise. CM Omar reiterated that the government’s commitment was to provide 200 units of free electricity to the poorest households. “I repeatedly explained in the Assembly that under the free electricity scheme, we would use solar panels to deliver this benefit to people,” he said. Taking on CM Omar heavily for his remarks, MLA Handwara Sajad Lone wrote on X: “Power tariffs in J&K cannot be suddenly compared to tariffs in other states at the pleasure of CM sahib. Power tariffs in J&K will be compared with tariffs in J&K in the past. What is this selective comparison. You didn’t make these comparisons during elections. And CM sahib has made a statement that he never said that he will not increase tariffs. To rejig CM sahib’s memory I am attaching the relevant page from NC election manifesto. The increase of 6.8% translates into an increase of more than 500 crores. This money has to be borne by the consumers. And these unsuspecting consumers were waiting for free 200 units of power per month, as promised by CM sahib in his Party’s election manifesto. This is not the first increase. In the non-metered areas, electric load per household was increased, thereby increasing the bill by about 10%. We did not hear a word about tariffs in other states during elections. And all we heard was the free 200 units of power per month. You had promised this free power for all. Once in power you said only AAY ration card holders will get it. That should be 200000 families approximately. CM sahib you have been in power for 22 months. You owe each consumer ( 22*200) 4400 units of power. That’s equal to 11000 rupees. And for 200000 AAY households that is equivalent to 2200000000, which is 2200 crores. CM sahib owes 2200 crores to the people and has the audacity to put a burden of 500 crores. Have some shame. Pay up. These are the poorest of the poor souls in J&K. You lied to them through your teeth. And on the basis of those lies rode to power”.

stories.headline: Power hike a compulsion, never promised rate won’t increase: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.title: Power hike a compulsion, never promised rate won’t increase: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 24: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday said there was no crisis in the government and maintained that any cabinet reshuffle would be carried out when he deemed it necessary, while defending the recent electricity tariff hike and calling for a thorough investigation into fresh threats to Kashmiri Pandit employees. “There is no crisis in the government. Our work is going on,” Abdullah said when asked about a possible reshuffle in his government. He said he had only ruled out a reshuffle before August 15 when asked about it earlier, and had not committed to carrying it out immediately afterwards. “I only told you that it would not happen before August 15. When it will happen and under what circumstances, leave that to me,” he said. On criticism from opposition parties over the increase in electricity tariffs, Abdullah said his government had never promised that power rates would not rise. He reiterated that the government’s commitment was to provide 200 units of free electricity to the poorest households. “I repeatedly explained in the Assembly that under the free electricity scheme, we would use solar panels to deliver this benefit to people,” he said. Abdullah argued that the tariff increase was separate from the free-power scheme and said the government had raised rates by only 6 per cent after four years. “We are not celebrating the increase in electricity rates. It was a compulsion for us,” he said, adding that lower power-sector losses would reduce the need for such measures in the future. On fresh threats reportedly targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees, Abdullah described the issue as a serious concern and urged the police and intelligence agencies to investigate their source. “Threats should not be coming at all,” he said, adding that the law-and-order and security agencies “should not take these things lightly”. He recalled that Pandit employees had been targeted under similar circumstances two to two-and-a-half years ago, saying the government had suffered “a great deal of loss” as a result. “Keeping all our employees safe and protecting them is a very major responsibility of the police,” Abdullah said. He also clarified that law and order was not his direct responsibility, saying the matter was handled by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha. “My advice to the law-and-order administration would be not to take this lightly. There should be a full investigation,” he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea By Tamil Nadu Law Officer Against Adverse Remarks Made By Madras HC
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea By Tamil Nadu Law Officer Against Adverse Remarks Made By Madras HC
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today issued notice on a plea by a Tamil Nadu Law Officer seeking expunction of adverse remarks made against him by the Madras High Court in an order concerning the conduct of a criminal trial.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta clarified that the notice would be limited to the observations made by the High Court against the petitioner.
The counsel appearing for the Law Officer submitted that no notice had been given to the petitioner before the High Court made the adverse observations.
Justice Mehta, however, questioned the submission, pointing out that the Law Officer had withheld a vital document from the trial court while prosecuting a criminal case.
“You exhibited the highest level of incompetence.
You don't deserve to be a public prosecutor.
Such a vital document you withheld.
Technically you may be right that no notice was given but you don't deserve any notice.
As a matter of fact, you don't deserve to be a public prosecutor,” Justice Mehta said.
The remarks challenged before the Supreme Court were made by Justice B. Pugalendhi of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on April 1, 2026.
The High Court was dealing with an application seeking suspension of the sentence of a person convicted in a case under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
During the hearing, the High Court found that the prosecution had failed to properly place before the trial court an Accident Register relating to the victim.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays HC Order Directing Kerala Govt To Refund Royalties Collected Under 2021 Kerala Minerals Act
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays HC Order Directing Kerala Govt To Refund Royalties Collected Under 2021 Kerala Minerals Act
stories.summary: The Court however restrained the State from collecting further royalties under the 2021 Act.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court however restrained the State from collecting further royalties under the 2021 Act.
The Supreme Court today stayed the Kerala High Court's direction for refund of the royalties collected by the Kerala government from landowners under the Kerala Minerals (Vesting of Rights) Act 2021.
The Court further ordered that the State shall not levy or recover any royalty under the Act until further orders.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order, while issuing notice on the Kerala government's challenge to the High Court order which declared the Act as "unconstitutional".

In the impugned order, the High Court examined the constitutional validity of the Kerala Minerals Act, which vested all rights in minerals beneath privately owned land in Malabar region in the State with retrospective effect from December 30, 2019.
While the Single Judge upheld the validity of the Act, a Division Bench declared it unconstitutional.

The Division Bench held that the State cannot vest ownership of privately owned mineral rights in itself without providing compensation or complying with the constitutional safeguards under Article 300A. Aggrieved, the State approached the Supreme Court.
Senior Advocate V Giri, for Kerala, argued that by virtue of the direction to refund the royalties, a huge burden has been imposed on a "small state" like Kerala.
When the CJI questioned the approximate burden which has fell upon the state, Giri replied, "about Rs.1200 crores".

Justice Bagchi observed that the State had a "public purpose" to make the law, but the question was, "when the state has a public purpose to make a law, and thereby vests certain properties, will it not be a part of the legislation to qualify the tests of Articles 14 and 19 to have some compensatory package?"
During the hearing, the CJI also asked if the State had plans to revisit the Act.
Subsequently, Giri contended that the State does not extract the minerals.

Justice Bagchi observed that the State had a "public purpose" to make the law, but the question was, "when the state has a public purpose to make a law, and thereby vests certain properties, will it not be a part of the legislation to qualify the tests of Articles 14 and 19 to have some compensatory package?" During the hearing, the CJI also asked if the State had plans to revisit the Act.

sentences.text: In the impugned order, the High Court examined the constitutional validity of the Kerala Minerals Act, which vested all rights in minerals beneath privately owned land in Malabar region in the State with retrospective effect from December 30, 2019.
The Supreme Court today stayed the Kerala High Court's direction for refund of the royalties collected by the Kerala government from landowners under the Kerala Minerals (Vesting of Rights) Act 2021.
The Court however restrained the State from collecting further royalties under the 2021 Act.

The Division Bench held that the State cannot vest ownership of privately owned mineral rights in itself without providing compensation or complying with the constitutional safeguards under Article 300A. Aggrieved, the State approached the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: JPSC exam row: Supreme Court seeks Centre, Jharkhand government's response on plea for CBI probe
stories.title: JPSC exam row: Supreme Court seeks Centre, Jharkhand government's response on plea for CBI probe
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre, Jharkhand government and others on a plea seeking a time-bound CBI probe into JPSC exam irregularities.

The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Centre, Jharkhand government and other authorities on a plea seeking an independent, impartial and time-bound CBI investigation into alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination 2025.

A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the Union of India, Jharkhand government, Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and other respondents.
Senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, told the bench that the plea seeks either a CBI probe or an inquiry by a former Supreme Court judge.
The petition was filed by activist Harisharan Devgan through advocate Satyam Singh Rajput.
It has raised concerns over the integrity, fairness, transparency and credibility of the preliminary examination conducted by the JPSC.

The petitioner has sought the transfer of the ongoing investigation from the state CID to the CBI, arguing that an independent agency is required to examine the alleged irregularities, including those involving public officials and examination agencies.
The plea said the controversy should not be viewed merely as a dispute involving individual candidates or isolated cases of alleged malpractice.
It has sought an examination of the entire examination process, from the preparation and printing of question papers to the handling and evaluation of answer sheets.

The petitioner has specifically sought scrutiny of the question paper preparation, coding, storage, transportation and distribution, as well as the conduct of the examination and the collection and custody of OMR sheets.

The plea also calls for examination of the scanning, coding and decoding of OMR sheets, evaluation, storage and access to electronic examination data, and the generation and publication of the results.
The petitioner has also asked the court to direct authorities to immediately secure all physical and digital evidence connected with the examination.

stories.headline: Supreme Court To Consider If Co-opting Ex-HC Judges As Women Bar Council Members Attracts Article 220 Restriction
stories.title: Supreme Court To Consider If Co-opting Ex-HC Judges As Women Bar Council Members Attracts Article 220 Restriction
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday said that it will consider whether co-opting former High Court Judges as women members in State Bar Councils will attract the bar under Article 220 of the Constitution, which prohibits a former High Court Judge from practising in that Court.
A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant heard the arguments raised by Senior Advocate Sanjay Parikh against the inclusion of a former High Court Judge.
Making an oral mention, Parikh, who was representing six Councils, submitted that the Supreme Court did not consider many aspects, such as the Dhulia committee reports, before passing the order.
Parikh asked if the Court can pass an order invoking Article 142 of the Constitution contrary to the Advocates Act.
The CJI replied that the Court was constrained to pass such an order as there were recurring repeated applications by various parties regarding the manner of implementing co-option.
"Every day there was a new application, new mentioning.
Every day new criteria was suggested and it was becoming very difficult," the CJI pointed out.
The CJI underscored that it was passed to ensure women's representation, which everyone welcomed.
Parikh, however submitted that a Constitutional issue could arise because, as per Article 220 of the Constitution, a retired High Court Judge cannot practice in the same Court.
Therefore, if a retired High Court Judge is made a member of the Bar Council, it could attract the bar under Article 220.
"The jurisdictional judge cannot practice.
So therefore, if a person who is barred from practice is made a member of the Advocates' body...," Parikh submitted.

stories.headline: Consider Amending Rule Barring Inter-State Transfer Of Death Row Convict : Supreme Court To Kerala
stories.title: Consider Amending Rule Barring Inter-State Transfer Of Death Row Convict : Supreme Court To Kerala
stories.summary: The Court cautioned that if the Rule is not amended, it might be struck down.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court cautioned that if the Rule is not amended, it might be struck down.

The Supreme Court today(August 24) directed the State of Kerala to file a counter-affidavit in a writ petition filed by Muhammed Ameer Ul Islam seeking transfer from prison in Kerala to a prison in his home State of Assam.
Islam, a migrant labourer from Assam, was convicted and sentenced to death in the 2016 Perumbavoor law student rape and murder case.

During the hearing, the bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu questioned the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services (Management) Rules, 2010, which disallow transfer of death convicts from one prison to another State contrary to the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950.
The bench asked the State of Kerala to consider amending the Rule.

Senior Advocate Rebecca John(for Islam) read Section 3 of the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950, and stated that prisoners sentenced to death are not allowed to be transferred unless the proceedings before the Trial Court and the High Court are over.
Referring to this, she pointed out that the Trial Court has already sentenced him to death, which was confirmed by the Kerala High Court in 2024.
On this, Justice Datta asked: "Where is the consent of Assam?"
John responded that the consent of the State of Assam is yet to come.
"Consent of Assam would come, but there is an outright refusal of Kerala.
Assam is saying we will consider if only Kerala allows," John said.

Referring to the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services (Management) Rules, Justice Datta asked if the petitioner has challenged Rule 587, which says that those sentenced to death are restricted from being transferred to prisons in other States.

stories.title: ICC penalises Jaiswal, Fernando with 25% match fee fine for heated exchange
stories.summary: India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka seamer Asitha Fernando were on Monday fined 25 per cent of their match fee for an on-field altercation on day one of the second Test in Colombo. The duo was also handed a demerit point each. The players were involved in a confrontation after Fernando dismissed Jaiswal in the 17th over of India's first innings. Jaiswal walked towards Fernando and the two exchanged words, following which Fernando moved his head towards Jaiswal. In response, Jaiswal leant in, resulting in their heads making contact.
